SUBJECT: packages/cli/src/adapters/FileSystemVaultAdapter.ts (walkDirectory + linkTextStaysInVault + realDirectoryBehind + realPathOrResolved). The sync-collection guard lives in a different file and has its own spec (`.sync-guard.spec.json`): the driver takes ONE subject. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). Every mutant is TYPE-PRESERVING. The axes read the REAL filesystem in a temp dir: the defect lives in what a real Dirent of a symlink answers, so a stubbed readdirSync would be vacuous. `expect` filled ONLY from a completed driver run.

N2_nested_rule_narrowed_to_inside_or_anc._note: Review round 3: the NARROW rule — a nested link is skipped only when its target lies inside the directory it sits in or contains it, and is judged normally otherwise. S21/S22 stay green under it (their targets are of exactly that kind); a sibling or unrelated target is followed again. Locks "never followed, whatever its target".

M17_file_link_passes_directory_check._note: Declared zero: a FILE link let through realDirectoryBehind is walked as a directory, readdir fails with ENOTDIR, and that failure is swallowed below a link — so S10 holds without this check (defensive). Canary M4 targets the same function.

_coverage._note_matrix: Measured, not predicted: every set comes from the driver's printed lists (control 0 red, rc=0). No two mutants share a red set (§A147). M1 (nothing followed) / M5 (plain subdirs under a link lost) / M11 (files under the REAL path) are told apart by S14, S15, S16, S19a.
_coverage._note_rule_layers: A link is judged twice: by its TEXT resolved from where it sits (linkTextStaysInVault) and by its RESOLVED target. M14 (text rule off) reddens only S18 — the one shape where the two disagree (a vault-relative link next to an outward assetspaces link). M3/M9 (resolved rules off) are reached by links whose text says nothing (a hop, a link opened through a linked root, another letter case). The ancestor half of the TEXT rule is defensive: where the text names an ancestor that exists, the resolved target is that ancestor too unless the path itself runs through a link — no mutant on it, stated.
_coverage._note_platform: S12 and S17 assert only on a case-INSENSITIVE filesystem and return early elsewhere: on Linux CI M8 and M13 are green by construction (macOS-only discriminators). M7 reddens S9 only where os.tmpdir() is itself a link (macOS /var → /private/var); on Linux M7 is still caught by S13. S21 reddens under M3 and M7 only on macOS for the same reason: elsewhere the TEXT rule already skips the original's absolute alias, so the resolved-target rule is not reached. ⚠ Consequence on Linux (derived, not measured there): M3 and M7 both reduce to [S13] — the "no two mutants share a red set" claim holds on macOS, where the driver ran.
_coverage._note_regression: D1-D3 (deterministic-vault-walk-193147b4) and FileSystemVaultAdapter.test.ts are in the harness: they stub readdirSync with Dirents answering true to isDirectory or isFile, so the new isSymbolicLink branch is never reached for them and no mutant reddens them — the old suites need no stub change.
_coverage._note_nested: Review round 2 (ticket 0a7ddb0d): a link BELOW a followed link is never followed. N1 removes that rule; it reddens S21 (an absolute alias inside the original's tree claims the real directory in a linked copy) and S22 (a link under `assetspaces` takes over the files of the vault's own later `inbox` link). Loops and diamonds inside an external tree are impossible by construction now; the visited set guards vault-level links only — S23 (two links to one directory) needs the check on the link (M2), S5 (a link to the parent of an already-walked one) also the check on plain sub-directories (M2b). S16 and S3 are no longer reddened by M2/M3/M7: their nested links are skipped by the nested rule before those checks are reached. Review round 3: N1 also reddens S24 (sibling target) and S25 (unrelated outward target); N2 (the narrow rule: skip only targets inside the link's directory or containing it) reddens exactly S24 S25 — S21/S22 alone did not lock the rule. S16 is held by the resolved-inside rule as well, so N1 leaves it green; its title claims only the hop back into the vault.
_coverage._note_unreddened: No mutant reddens S4 or S10, by construction: S4's inside link is caught by BOTH the text rule and the resolved-target rule (a single mutant removes one, the other holds), and S10's file link is held twice as well — the isDirectory check in realDirectoryBehind is defensive, since a followed file link would fail readdir with ENOTDIR, which is swallowed below a link.
